sumInsured: Not specified in provided extract (Base Sum Insured as per Policy Schedule)

great.name: Restore benefit (Automatic Recharge) – covers same & different illnesses
great.quote: The Recharge shall be available for same illness as well different illnesses.
great.explanation: This is a strong restore/recharge: once your eligible sum insured is exhausted, the policy reinstates up to Base Sum Insured and it can be used even for the same illness (not just unrelated illnesses).

great.name: Built-in additional Sum Insured buffer – Automatic Recharge up to Base SI (once/year)
great.quote: The Company agrees to automatically make the re-instatement of up to the Base Sum Insured once in a policy year
great.explanation: Provides extra usable coverage after the base pool is exhausted (subject to conditions), improving protection in a high-claim year.

great.name: Modern/advanced treatments covered (as listed) up to Base SI
great.quote: The Company will indemnify the Insured Person up to Base Sum Insured for expenses incurred ... for treatment taken through following advance technology methods: ... Robotic surgeries ... Stereotactic radio surgeries ... Immunotherapy- Monoclonal Antibody ...
great.explanation: Explicit coverage for multiple modern treatment methods under hospitalization, without stating a monetary sub-limit for each listed method (payable up to Base Sum Insured).

good.name: Pre-existing disease (PED) waiting period – 36 months
good.quote: Expenses related to the treatment of a pre-existing Disease (PED) ... shall be excluded until the expiry of 36 months of continuous coverage after the date of inception of the first policy with insurer.
good.explanation: PED waiting of 3 years is within the acceptable/standard range in India (not a red flag). Optional cover can reduce it to 24 months.

good.name: Specific illness waiting period – 24 months
good.quote: Expenses related to the treatment of the listed Conditions, surgeries/treatments shall be excluded until the expiry of 24 months of continuous coverage after the date of inception of the first policy with the Company.

good.name: Initial waiting period – 30 days
good.quote: Expenses related to the treatment of any illness within 30 days from the first policy commencement date shall be excluded except claims arising due to an accident
good.explanation: Standard 30-day initial waiting for illnesses (accidents covered).

good.name: Room rent – Single Private Room (default as per wording; final eligibility as per Policy Schedule)
good.quote: If the Policy Schedule states 'Single Private Room' as eligible Room Category, it means the maximum eligible Room Category ... is limited to stay in a Single Private Room.
good.explanation: Single Private AC room is industry-standard. Note: the actual room eligibility depends on what your Policy Schedule shows; the wording also allows variants like 'up to 1% of Base SI per day' or 'no limit' via optional cover.

good.name: Domiciliary hospitalization covered (home treatment) – if opted/available in schedule
good.quote: Benefit 6 : Domiciliary Hospitalization The Company will indemnify the Insured Person ... for the Medical Expenses incurred towards Domiciliary Hospitalization
good.explanation: Home hospitalization is covered subject to conditions and limits per Policy Schedule.

good.name: Optional cover trade-off: Smart Select gives premium discount; extra co-pay only if you go outside listed hospitals
good.quote: If this Optional Cover is opted, then Policyholder is entitled for a discount of 15% on the Premium payable... If the Insured Person takes Medical Treatment in hospitals other than those listed in Annexure – IV ... shall bear a Co-Payment of 20% on each and every Claim
good.explanation: This is an optional plan choice: you can accept network-based restrictions for a discount, or avoid the optional cover to avoid this extra co-pay.

bad.name: Consumables / non-medical items not covered (customer pays out-of-pocket)
bad.quote: Any item or condition or treatment specified in List of Non-Medical Items (Annexure – II to Policy Terms & Conditions).
bad.reference: Clause 4.2(1) and Annexure II (List of Expenses Generally Excluded)
bad.explanation: Consumables/non-medical items (e.g., gloves, masks, syringes, many kits/bundles) are excluded, which can materially increase hospital bill out-of-pocket.

bad.name: Pre-hospitalization cover limited to 30 days
bad.quote: Under Relevant Pre-hospitalization Medical Expenses, for a period of 30 days immediately prior to the Insured Person's date of admission
bad.explanation: 30 days is on the lower side vs better plans that offer >60 days.

bad.name: Post-hospitalization cover limited to 60 days
bad.quote: Under Relevant Post-hospitalization Medical Expenses, for a period of 60 days immediately after the Insured Person's date of discharge
bad.explanation: 60 days is on the lower side vs better plans that offer >180 days.

bad.name: No Claims Bonus (NCB) reduces after a claim (not protected)
bad.quote: In the event of a Claim occurring during any Policy Year, the accrued No Claims Bonus will be reduced by 10% of the Base Sum Insured at the commencement of next Policy Year
bad.explanation: The renewal bonus is not fully protected; it reduces after a claim, which is weaker than non-reducing/non-resetting bonus structures.

bad.name: Disease-wise monetary sub-limits possible if mentioned in Policy Schedule (can cap payouts for major procedures)
bad.quote: The Company will indemnify the Insured Person for Medical Expenses incurred in respect of the below mentioned Ailments / Procedures up to the amount specified against each and every Ailment /Procedure mentioned in the Policy Schedule ... (These conditions will apply only if specifically mentioned in the Policy Schedule)
bad.explanation: If your Policy Schedule includes these sub-limits (cataract, hernia, knee replacement, etc.), claims for those treatments can be capped at stated amounts, reducing effective coverage.

unclear.name: Co-pay (base policy) – only if specified in Policy Schedule (not stated as 0% here)
unclear.quote: The Co-payment, if and as specified in the Policy Schedule, shall be borne by the Policyholder / Insured Person on each Claim
unclear.reference: Clause 3(g) – General Conditions Applicable To All Benefits And Optional Covers
unclear.explanation: The base plan co-pay (0% or any %) is not explicitly stated in the provided extract because it depends on your Policy Schedule. Confirm your schedule to know if co-pay applies.

unclear.name: Cashless network size (number of network hospitals) not stated
unclear.quote: For an updated list of Network Providers ... the Insured Person may refer to the list of Network Providers available on the Company's website or at the call center.
unclear.explanation: The document doesn’t mention how many network hospitals exist (e.g., 7,000/10,000+). You’ll need to verify the current network count from the insurer.

disclaimer: Standard IRDAI exclusions apply. Please verify all details with your insurer or policy document.
